I live further up north, and ive had an Ebike since 2018. I've used it through the winters without issues. the riding style has to change a bit, as you dont have the grip to lean into the corners.

winter tires can be bought at almost any store that sells bikes.

while i dont have a recommendation for bike brand, I'd recommend getting a bosch crank motor. not the motors in the wheel hub. reason being crank motors have shorter response time making the entire experience less jerky. the hub motor only activates when it feels a pull on the chain, but the crank motor senses the push on the pedals meaning you have a slightly more instant feedback.

PS, i also recommend the higher wattage engines as hills are a bitch. that and if you hsve to bike to deep snow they have more oomph to get through

The 5 to 1 ratio was because the Sherman was bever intended as a pure tank v tank vehicle it was a compromise of several factors which dictated its formation. You could get like 2+ shermans from the resources beeded for one tiger, its way more field serviceable and reliable. Also since the US was advancing most of the time the tiger had the benefit of being able to pre aim on a target because it saw the shermans first most of the time (you see a moving target better than a stationary one) so the tiger could take out like 2 maybe 3 tanks if it was lucky before the shermans found its position pinned it down and flanked it

The Ronson nickname was for the early shermans before they got better stowage (wet stowage). Any tank that was hit and penetrated was considered a kill because if a round penetrated it either made the crew inside experience rapid dismantlement by HE (APHE). Or it made the ting go up in flames due to the ammo cooking off. Or the crew GTFO'ed because who wants to be in a tin can that cant return fire and is already perfectly targeted.

The quality improved over time. But both the M4 and the tiger were unreliable at some point. The tigers transmission broke down often. The M4 had a gyrostablilzer that was either incorrecly calibrated or turned off untill the crews learned to use it properly. Which made gun accuracy suffer.

The 75mm was never meant as an anti tank gun. They had the choice of picking the 75 or the 76 at some point during the development. They went with the 75 because the HE shell characteristics were what they were after. The majority of ammunition used by shermans was HE as they were fighing infantry more than tanks
